gaps.what: Who held Kham and Amdo 1354-1641: the shapes are cut to Ü-Tsang but no page opened names the holders (Ming commissions on paper, the Beri king in 1640-41); also who administered Kham after 1641 (Khoshut page silent)
Rulers 1432-1565 (Rinpungpa period) and 1642-1951 (Dalai Lamas and regents): the ruler strip has a 133-year gap and stops in 1642
Tsangpa reach 1565-1620: the Tsangpa page puts the conquest of Ü in 1618-1620 (Kyishö and Tsal 1618, Nêdong 1620) and gives Dagpo, Phanyul and Neu no date, but the shape holds all of Ü from 1354
1865 change on the Dri River boundary (Nyarong) not ledgered; page to try: Xinlong County
Tawang claim and the area south of the Sela Pass after 1947 (ledger 1947 at confidence 1); page to try: McMahon Line
1930-32 Tibetan advance east of the Yangtze (Dege, Garze) not drawn; net zero by 1933
Who held Chamdo and western Kham in 1912-1917 (the page names no holder; the occupation by the Republic is a reading, confidence 1)

Cliopatria's 1734-1775 shapes hold 200 cells in the Himalayan south (Arunachal side) that the 1683-1726 keyframes leave out, so they enter at 1727 without an event; 92 Central Tibet cells at the Aksai Chin and Arunachal edges fall out at 1642 without an event
Ming relations (tribute from 1373, titles of 1372 and 1406) and the Khoshut, Qing and PRC protectorate tints are not ledgered here; vassal events belong to the suzerain's dossier

problems: ORCHESTRATOR DECISION (F2): tibet now books Kham as a 1642 gain with counterpart khoshut-khanate and keeps Kokonor and the Qaidam Basin (the 921 northern cells of Cliopatria's plateau) out of every Tibet shape 1642-1726. khoshut-khanate must carry the mirror: a 1642 loss/transfer of Kham to 'tibet' (it books Kham as its own gain from Beri in 1641 and keeps Kham, Central Tibet and Qinghai in its keyframes to 1717, so the map would paint Kham twice). The alternative is the protectorate model (Tibet holds the plateau, Kokonor included, under a Khoshut suzerain): then khoshut-khanate's 1641/1642 gains become vassal events counterpart 'tibet' and tibet_1642 to tibet_1721 regain the 921 cells. Either way khoshut-khanate's 1642-03 gain of Central Tibet from tsangpa-dynasty (= tibet, no separate dossier) conflicts with tibet's 1642 rename.

The 1724 Qinghai province (Kokonor/Qaidam, 921 cells) is no longer a Tibetan loss and no dossier of this group books it: khoshut-khanate ends in 1717 (dissolve), so the Kokonor land 1717-1724 and its passage to qing-dynasty need an owner (khoshut-khanate keyframes to 1724, or qing-dynasty, or nobody).

dzungar-khanate books Central Tibet as a 1717 gain and a 1720 loss to qing-dynasty; tibet books the same years as an occupation (types differ, years agree). qing-dynasty should carry vassal_start 1720 / vassal_end 1912 with counterpart 'tibet'.

Gazetteer: 'Central Tibet' resolves to the whole Tibet Autonomous Region (Chamdo and Ngari included); every dossier using it for historical Ü-Tsang (tibet, khoshut-khanate, dzungar-khanate) inherits about 220,000 km2 of Chamdo and Ngari. A separate U-Tsang region is needed; tibet now writes it as a minus.
The validator accepts only two operands in a minus; the reviewer's three-operand suggestion was written nested.
Circles for Latö (86.9 E 29.0 N, 100 km), Mangyül Gungthang (85.5 E 28.4 N, 90 km) and Guge (79.8 E 31.5 N, 150 km) are the author's placements; no page opened gives boundaries.
